name: options-for-a-vector-store
query: We need a vector store for about two million chunks and we're OSS-only. What are my options?
why: The canonical read-path options question. The skill surveys the retrieval layer of the bundled map with the OSS framing before recommending one path, and nothing is being built yet.

name: is-it-still-maintained
query: Is LangGraph still actively maintained, or has that project gone quiet?
why: A maintenance-status question asked to inform a decision. Answered from the dated corpus with its as-of date, never from training memory.

name: what-does-this-license-oblige
query: If we ship a commercial product on top of that AGPL vector database, what does the license actually oblige us to do?
why: License judgment on a catalogued component. License traps are one of the things the read path owns, and the answer comes from the corpus row, not recall.

name: review-a-proposed-architecture
query: Here's the design for our support copilot: every user turn re-embeds the whole conversation and fans out to three separate indexes. Does that hold up?
why: Architecture review against the engineering principles. No new components are being chosen and no repo is being generated, so it stays on the read path.

name: log-what-broke
query: Note that the install for that vector DB fails on Python 3.13 - we hit it twice today.
why: Write mode's RECORD job. First-hand experience with a catalogued tool, with the version condition that makes the note falsifiable rather than an opinion.

name: discover-new-tools
query: Any new agent frameworks worth adding? Give the tooling catalog a refresh pass.
why: Write mode's DISCOVER job: scan the seed sources, confirm each candidate, then dedupe-ingest through ledger.py rather than pasting links in by hand.

name: check-for-staleness
query: Check the AI catalog for staleness - which entries haven't been verified in the last three months?
why: Write mode's VERIFY job on both axes: liveness probing that URLs still resolve, and the more valuable claims queue on map rows whose assertions are unverified.

name: documented-flag-does-not-exist
query: That flag the docs told us to pass doesn't exist in the current release. Second time this week their docs have been wrong.
why: The hardest write-mode positive: no maintenance pass was asked for and there is no explicit request at all, but a tool in the corpus was used and something was learned, which is exactly when a note gets recorded.

name: build-me-an-agent
query: Build me an agent that watches our contracts folder and summarizes anything new that lands in it.
why: Build mode's core request. Intake runs first, the stack is committed slot by slot, and the run may rightly conclude that a scheduled script beats an agent.

name: add-an-ai-feature-to-an-existing-app
query: Add an AI feature to our Rails app that suggests tags for each post as the author writes it.
why: Adding an AI subsystem to an existing repo is build mode's job. The existing footprint becomes an intake constraint rather than a reason to skip intake.

name: stack-for-a-committed-build
query: We've committed to building a document-extraction service this quarter. Which stack should we use?
why: The hardest build-mode positive. It is phrased like a read-path options question, but a specific system is being built, so it needs intake and a committed stack rather than a survey of options.

name: research-a-tool-from-scratch
query: Research the state of open-weight embedding models thoroughly and come back with sources and dates.
why: Belongs to deep-research. The subject is AI tooling, but the request is for multi-angle verified web research, which this skill delegates rather than performs; folding the result in afterward goes to write mode.

name: concurrency-bug-with-an-llm-in-it
query: Our FastAPI endpoint that calls the LLM times out under load. How do I fix the concurrency?
why: General software engineering with an AI label on it, so it routes to agent-skills. No component is being chosen and no tooling claim is in question.

name: write-an-mcp-server
query: Write an MCP server that exposes our internal ticketing API.
why: Belongs to build-mcp-server. This skill can say which MCP servers fit a stack, but MCP scaffolding is never hand-rolled here.

name: scaffold-a-plain-web-app
query: Scaffold a new Next.js dashboard for our internal metrics.
why: General application work with no AI subsystem, so it routes to agent-skills. Guards against firing on the word scaffold alone.

name: update-a-project-readme
query: Update our README to describe the new agent module we added.
why: Ordinary documentation work in the user's own project, which goes to agent-skills. Write mode only ever touches the shared tooling corpus under resources/, so this guards against firing on the verb update near the word agent.

name: refresh-a-data-catalog
query: Our data catalog has stale table descriptions. Can we refresh them?
why: A warehouse metadata chore, not the AI tooling corpus. Shares the words catalog, stale and refresh with write mode and shares nothing else.
